occurrences.text:
The next inquiry I would put is a criterion question, not a verdict on J or on the criticism: **what distinguishes a presupposition the description relies on from an expressive limit the description cannot draw, and on which side of that line does P9’s cross-booking compatibility objection fall independently of how J or J′ phrases it?**

That inquiry is warranted by two frozen source occurrences. P7, the excerpt on criticism targets, already names “the assumption that logical time is meaningful” as an object of criticism. That is not a record the snapshot carries; it is an assumption the description relies on. P9, the excerpt on local alternatives, global availability, and the conditional compatibility objection, says that intervals lose correlations, that booking A’s high alternative “might be incompatible” with booking B’s high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot, and then glosses that “the snapshot does not name physical resources, so this incompatibility is invisible.” The uncertainty is whether that gloss is part of the objection or a separate meta-observation, and whether P7’s “snapshot as a whole” is a claim-level target that can absorb an expressive-limit criticism or only covers inconsistency and aggregation of carried claims.

The criticism C makes the first unresolved issue sharp: J’s announced split between criticizing a carried commitment and criticizing an absent one is too broad, because P7’s fifth item is already an assumption the description does not carry. J′ responds by narrowing the distinction to presupposition the description makes versus expressive limit the description cannot state. But J′ leaves open whether “snapshot as a whole” can cover the expressive-limit version, and it does not supply a test for deciding when a criticism belongs to one side rather than the other. Without that test, J′ may have relabeled the defect rather than corrected it.

Different outcomes would change the proposed use in different ways. If a criterion shows that P7’s “snapshot as a whole” or its assumption target already covers expressive-limit criticisms, then J′’s added category is unnecessary for P7/P9. The compatibility objection would remain locatable in P7’s taxonomy once its factual condition is met, and the proposed use would reduce to a scope clarification — marginal summary versus joint feasibility — plus the repair-asymmetry point about local versus joint loss. If instead a criterion shows that expressive-limit criticisms are not covered by any P7 target, then J′ must retain an explicit new target or classify the compatibility objection as a vocabulary-adequacy claim rather than a criticism of a record, rule, history, or snapshot. The proposed use would then carry a genuine taxonomy extension, not merely a sharper division inside the existing one. If no criterion can be derived from the frozen material, then the correction remains provisional: the compatibility objection stays conditionally locatable only under its factual reading, and its expressive-limit aspect remains unresolved rather than absorbed by “snapshot as a whole.”

Several existing claims and uses should remain distinguishable throughout. Criticism of a rule is not criticism of a record, a booking history, a snapshot, or an assumption. Accepting and rejecting rules and data can combine differently, and the compatibility objection can be raised while accepting every rule and delivered record. P9’s cross-booking incompatibility remains a conditional possibility, not an observation, until a resource-sharing relation and an incompatible assignment are supplied. Local alternative loss, aggregation, bounds, and cross-booking correlation have different roles; the repair asymmetry — keeping per-booking alternatives addresses the local loss but not the joint loss — is not the same as merely naming an interval construction and a correlation loss. Exposing alternatives and objecting to downstream resolution remain disputed positions, not settled by J′. E009 remains an unendorsed prior model occurrence rather than warehouse evidence; J remains a historical construct occurrence; J′ is a proposed successor, not an amendment to P7, P9, or either candidate language. And the two missing observations — a warehouse resource-sharing relation, and what the consumer of availability actually asks — remain distinct in kind from the criterion inquiry itself.

This next inquiry does not certify whether C’s criticism bears. It asks whether J′’s narrower distinction can bear the weight C places on it. If it cannot, the appropriate response is not to accept a diagnosis or reject a target, but to keep the factual and expressive-limit readings of P9’s compatibility objection separately open.
